title: Sold option premium is a distribution from your future self, not income
summary: Selling covered calls and cash-secured puts does not create income from nothing. The speaker compares it with a fund's distribution yield, which mixes income with returned capital gains; SEC yield is the more honest number. Premium is paid out of your future returns. He still sells calls, but only when paid enough.

steps.caption: Own 100 shares at $100 and sell a $105 call, one month out.
The legs: long stock and a short call.
The covered call at expiry: premium added, gains capped at the strike.
The cap: above $105 every further gain belongs to the call buyer.
The premium lowers breakeven a little. That is the 'income'.
Below breakeven you carry almost all the stock's downside.

takeaways: Premium is a payment from your future upside, not free income.
Like distribution yield versus SEC yield, the headline number can mislead.
Sell premium when it pays enough for the tradeoff.
caveats: The transcript is partly cut. Promotional: link in bio.
